idiom_name: component instanceof TextAccessor ta; default methods for additive growth
implementation_notes: A Java interface is the extension contract, and because a class's interface list is fixed at compile time the runtime probe is the whole lookup: if (component instanceof TextAccessor ta) discriminates and binds in one step (Java 16+), and absence is an ordinary false. Java 8 default methods relieve the additive case - a shipped interface can gain members without breaking implementors - and java.util.ServiceLoader discovers implementations contributed by other jars, covering external extensions without a registry of your own; use the adapter-manager variant when an extension must be handed out for a type you do not own.
pitfalls: Adding an abstract method to a published interface breaks every implementor at compile time (and throws AbstractMethodError for stale classes); use default methods or a new interface - the rule the pattern exists to satisfy.
String-based adapters (getAdapter(String className)) bypass the type system and only resolve when the contributing bundle is already activated; prefer Class<T>-keyed lookups.
Adapters cached per adaptable must be released with it, and a factory that creates a new adapter per call churns or leaks.
instanceof cannot see interfaces added by dynamic proxies unless they were declared when the proxy was created, so a probe can miss proxy-supplied extensions.

variants.name: IAdaptable + adapter factories (Eclipse Platform)
variants.implementation_notes: The plug-in-scale realization of the pattern: the adaptable object funnels getAdapter(Class<T>) to an adapter manager, which forwards the request to registered adapter factories and returns null when no factory can produce the type, so extensions can be attached to types that cannot be edited and contributed declaratively by plug-ins. Clients use the documented three-step lookup - does the object implement the interface, then IAdaptable.getAdapter, then AdapterManager.getAdapter/loadAdapter - with loadAdapter activating the contributing plug-in (and therefore used sparingly).
pitfalls: getAdapter never activates the contributing plug-in, so a declaratively registered factory is invisible until something else loads it - use loadAdapter only when activation is acceptable.
The adapter manager is global shared state keyed by adaptable type: factories leak if they are registered and never unregistered.
Adapters created per call must be cached on the adaptable (or the factory) or every lookup allocates anew.
